title: Cell structure
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.1.1-c19 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.1.1-c18 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.1.1.3-xt1 term and clue written for the game; 4.1.1-c20 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.1.1-q07, 4.1.1-q08, 4.1.1-q10, 4.1.1-q12, 4.1.1-x02 (written for the game), 4.1.1-q09, 4.1.1-q11, 4.1.1-q14, 4.1.1-x03 (written for the game), 4.1.1-q15, 4.1.1-q16, 4.1.1-q13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Culture medium
items.clue: The nutrients supplied for growing microorganisms.

items.label: Binary fission
items.clue: The simple cell division by which bacteria multiply.

items.label: Sperm cell
items.clue: The male gamete, with a tail for swimming towards the egg

items.label: Aseptic technique
items.clue: The set of precautions used to prepare an uncontaminated culture.

questions.stem: Root hair cells have a long, thin extension that reaches out into the soil. How does this help the cell to carry out its function?

options.text: It makes the cell larger so it can work faster.
It exposes the chloroplasts to more sunlight.
It allows a thicker cellulose wall to form.
It increases the surface area for absorption.

questions.explanation: The structure of the root hair cell relates to its function in the plant: the extension gives a large surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions from the soil.

questions.stem: Which statement about cell differentiation is correct?

options.text: Most animal cells differentiate at an early stage.
Most plant cells differentiate at an early stage.
Most cells differentiate by growing to a bigger size.
Most animal cells differentiate to repair damage.

questions.explanation: As an organism develops, cells differentiate to form different types of cell, and most types of animal cell differentiate at an early stage.

questions.stem: Why can an electron microscope be used to study cells in much finer detail than a light microscope?

options.text: It magnifies the image very many more times.
It has higher magnification and resolution.
It finds the real size from the image size.
It uses a much stronger lens to enlarge cells.

questions.explanation: An electron microscope has much higher magnification and resolving power than a light microscope, so it can be used to study cells in much finer detail.

questions.stem: One bacterium divides once every 20 minutes. How many bacteria will there be after 2 hours?

options.text: 12 bacteria
64 bacteria
7 bacteria
120 bacteria

questions.explanation: There are 6 divisions in 2 hours at one division every 20 minutes, and the population doubles each time, so the number is 1 × 2⁶ = 64.

questions.stem: A sperm cell has many mitochondria packed into its middle section. How does this help the cell to carry out its function?

options.text: They carry the genetic information to the egg
They digest a way through the egg's outer layer
They transfer the energy needed for swimming
They make the proteins that build the tail

questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out respiration, transferring the energy the tail needs to swim to the egg.

questions.stem: In a mature animal, what is cell division mainly used for?

options.text: Cell division has stopped in mature animals.
Cell division makes the cells grow larger.
Cell division repairs and replaces cells.
Cell division continues as the animal grows.

questions.explanation: In mature animals, cell division is mainly restricted to repair and replacement.

questions.stem: The image of a cell is 10 mm wide. The real cell is 0.05 mm wide. What is the magnification?
questions.explanation: magnification = size of image / size of real object = 10 mm / 0.05 mm = 200. Both measurements are in the same units, so the magnification has no units.

questions.stem: Why should cultures be incubated at a maximum temperature of 25°C in a school laboratory?

options.text: It reduces the growth of harmful pathogens.
It is the temperature for fastest growth.
It stops condensation forming on the lid.
It matches the body temperature of humans.

questions.explanation: In school and college laboratories cultures are incubated at a maximum of 25°C, because this reduces the likelihood of growing pathogens that could harm people.

questions.stem: A gardener cuts a short piece of stem from a plant. In damp soil it grows roots and becomes a new plant. What does this show?

options.text: Many plant cells keep the ability to differentiate
Plant cells can differentiate only inside a seed
The piece of stem already had hidden root cells
Plant cells grow without needing to differentiate

questions.explanation: Many plant cells can differentiate throughout life, so cells in a cut stem can form new roots.

questions.stem: Why is a Petri dish stored upside down after the agar gel has been inoculated?

options.text: To stop the agar falling out of the dish.
To stop condensation dripping onto the agar.
To keep the culture warm enough to grow.
To hold the lid firmly against the agar.

questions.explanation: With the dish upside down, condensation collects on the lid below the agar gel and cannot drip onto its surface, so the culture stays uncontaminated.

questions.stem: A clear area around a colony on an agar plate is 20 mm across. What is its cross-sectional area?

options.text: 314 mm²
1257 mm²
63 mm²
31.4 mm²

questions.explanation: The radius is half of 20 mm, so r = 10 mm and the cross-sectional area is πr² = π × 10² = 314 mm².

questions.stem: One bacterium divides once every 20 minutes. What is the number of bacteria after 5 hours, expressed in standard form?
questions.explanation: 5 hours gives 15 divisions, so the number is 2¹⁵ = 32 768, which is 3.3 × 10⁴ to two significant figures in standard form.
